verdicts.summary: Prompts queued while no dialog is mounted are never pruned when they expire. Only the head can be removed, so stale expired prompts sit in front of a live prompt.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Desktop is on /pair, /connect, the guest page or the sign-in screen; root renders only <Outlet/> there, so SshPasswordPromptDialog is not mounted (__root.tsx:165-212, dialog only at :239). 2) Two or more SSH prompts arrive and are appended by startSshPasswordPromptQueue (SshPasswordPromptDialog.tsx:51-52); one expires meanwhile. 3) Later the shell mounts and the dialog shows queue[0], which is expired. 4) removeSshPasswordPrompt only removes the head (:67), and there is no expiry sweep, so the user must click Dismiss on each stale prompt (:134-136, :211-213) before reaching the live one. 5) The dialog also opens with 'Expired' even though the user never saw the prompt.
verdicts.consequence: Stale 'SSH verification required / Expired' dialogs appear in sequence after sign-in or pairing, and a live prompt is hidden behind them. The queue also grows without bound while the dialog is unmounted. The old code dropped such prompts, so this is new.

verdicts.summary: The new Escape observer runs before the `_chat` route's Escape handler that clears the sidebar thread selection, so Escape on /pull-requests with a selection leaves the page instead of clearing it.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Multi-select threads in the sidebar, then open /pull-requests. It sits under the `_chat` layout, which mounts ChatRouteGlobalShortcuts (_chat.tsx:221). 2) Press Escape. 3) The dispatcher's window bubble listener was installed at the first registerCommands call, before `_chat`'s later window listener (dispatcher.ts:87-92, _chat.tsx:175). It therefore runs first. 4) runScopes finds no scope that consumes Escape, so consumed=false. 5) The observer at AppSidebarLayout.tsx:179-190 calls preventDefault and navigates back or home. 6) `_chat`'s handler then hits `if (event.defaultPrevented) return` (_chat.tsx:72), so clearSelection (:88-91) never runs. Before the change, the page's own listener registered after `_chat`'s, so `_chat` cleared the selection and preventDefault made the page skip leaving. The comment at AppSidebarLayout.tsx:173-174 says a selection claims Escape, but that handler is not a dispatcher scope, so it cannot claim it.
verdicts.consequence: Escape on the pull requests page with a thread selection leaves the page and keeps the selection. Before, the first Escape cleared the selection and the second left the page.

verdicts.summary: The keepAlive atom probes once and falls back to ['vscode'] on rejection, an empty result or a missing bridge, as the old hook did.
verdicts.scenario: I tried to make the probe run twice or lose its result. A re-read after the atom is disposed would re-probe, and a late setSelf would be dropped. Neither is possible: the atom has no dependencies and is keepAlive. A rejected probe is swallowed by the second `then` handler, and an empty result never calls setSelf, so the fallback stays.

verdicts.summary: The pre-auth question is answered: shell atoms were already mounted before auth. The remaining risk is that the visit migration now runs earlier on cached shells, and I could not read whether its command fails when the environment is not yet connected.
verdicts.scenario: Pre-auth: AppRoot's mount effect already subscribes to environmentThreadShells.threadRefsAtom and environmentShell.stateAtom on appAtomRegistry (AppRoot.tsx:16-25, composerDraftStore.ts:4119-4152). That chain reaches environmentThreadsAtom and snapshotAtom for every enabled environment, outside the auth gate. So the new subscriptions do not newly start shell subscriptions or supervisors, and the first reviewer's open question is not a new hazard. Remaining: startThreadVisitedMigration subscribes with immediate:true at page start (useThreadVisitedMigration.ts:37-39). It adds each thread key to migratedThreadKeys before the command runs (:21-22) and ignores failure (:29-34, reportFailure:false). If a cached shell emits before the environment connects and the visit command rejects, that key is never retried for the page's life. The old hook had the same mark-before-send logic, but it ran only after auth. I did not read the runInEnvironment, supervisor and visitThread code that decides whether the command waits or fails. Also, announcements while the region is unattached advance memory and are dropped, as the note says.
verdicts.consequence: If the command fails when the environment is offline, a local visit time is not handed to the server and the thread may keep showing a stale server-side visit state until the next page load.
